s1.syndrome_frame: bilateral breast lumps with rapid onset and varying characteristics, associated with lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: left breast lump fixed to the chest wall
irregular spiculated mass in the left breast on MRI
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
regular menstrual cycles
left breast lump: 4 × 4 cm, hard, fixed to the chest wall
right breast lump: 1 × 1 cm, firm, mobile
MRI showed irregular spiculated mass in the left breast
MRI showed well-defined lesion in the right breast
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy on MRI
ultrasound and bone scan were negative for metastases
fine-needle aspiration cytology of the left breast lump showed malignant cells
FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showed malignant cells
core-needle biopsy of the left breast confirmed infiltrative duct cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Bilateral invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by core-needle biopsy and FNAC

shortlist.label: Bilateral invasive lobular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given bilateral breast lumps and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Lymphoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy and lymphoma is a rare but possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Fibroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Right breast lump characteristics and suspected diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral breast lumps with malignant cells on fine-needle aspiration cytology, particularly the left breast lump showing poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism and the core-needle biopsy confirming infiltrative duct cell carcinoma, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of characteristic inflammatory signs such as erythema, edema, or warmth of the breast skin.

rejected.label: Bilateral invasive lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: The cytology and biopsy results specifically mention ductal cells, not lobular cells, which are characteristic of lobular carcinoma.

rejected.label: Lymphoma of the breast
rejected.why: The fine-needle aspiration cytology and core-needle biopsy results do not indicate lymphoma, which would typically show a distinct lymphocytic population.

rejected.label: Fibroadenoma
rejected.why: While the right breast lump was initially suspected to be a fibroadenoma based on its characteristics, the presence of malignant cells in the left breast and the overall clinical picture do not support fibroadenoma as the primary diagnosis for both breasts.
